sources.entry: AI Footprint - Read-only menu bar app that shows the disk space, background processes, MCP servers and login items AI coding tools leave on your Mac, with a receipt for every update. summary.name: AI Footprint
summary.one_liner: A free, open-source, read-only macOS menu bar app that shows the disk space, running processes, orphaned MCP servers and login items left behind by AI coding tools.
keywords: see what ai tools installed mac
use_cases: Finding how much disk space local AI models and caches use on a Mac
Spotting orphaned MCP server processes still using memory
Checking which AI tools are set to start at login
Reviewing what changed after an AI tool updated
Auditing background processes left by AI coding assistants
summary.what_it_does: Reports disk usage per tool and per folder for Claude Code, the Claude app, Codex, Ollama, LM Studio and Hugging Face, including models, caches, logs, transcripts, virtual machines and installed versions. Lists each tool's running processes with memory use and what keeps them running, such as an app, terminal, login item, or nothing. Flags MCP servers still running after their parent app quit. Shows login items that tools set to start at login or restart when quit. Checks every 15 minutes and keeps update receipts recording version changes, disk changes and login item changes. It never deletes or stops anything; it offers Show in Finder and a Copy Stop Command for Terminal that is shown before copying.
notable: Read-only: never deletes or stops anything; stop commands are shown for the user to copy
Flags orphaned MCP servers that keep running with nothing connected
Update receipts record version, disk and login item changes after tool updates
Open source, with no internet access and a SECURITY.md describing data handling
caveats: Only covers the AI tools it lists (Claude Code, Claude app, Codex, Ollama, LM Studio, Hugging Face)
Update receipts depend on the app staying running, since it checks every 15 minutes
